_comment: Example config for the urgency axis (Phase 2 of the personal-assistant expansion, T-20260704-02). Copy to config/urgency.json (gitignored, site-specific, same pattern as config/domains.json) and adjust to your own setup. Urgency is DELIBERATELY decoupled from the 5-dimension complexity score in the main prompt (Clarity/Complexity/Creativity/Context/Criticality) -- a ticket can be low-complexity (Tier 1, fast to fix) and still urgent (fix it now), or high-complexity and not urgent (queue it).

urgency_definitions.sofort: Dispatch a sub-agent immediately -- or, if severity is unclear, at least a lean diagnosis-only sub-agent to size the issue before committing to a fix. No queueing.
urgency_definitions.heute: Handle within the same day; fine to wait for the next natural check-in.
urgency_definitions.woche: Handle within the week; fine to sit with a companion sub-agent or the later_sink for a while.
urgency_definitions.backlog: No deadline pressure. Route straight to the later_sink (or the project's own task management if none is configured) instead of spawning a sub-agent.

domain_defaults._comment: Keyed by domain id from config/domains.json (see domains.example.json for the schema; ids like 'alltag'/'gesundheit'/'buero'/'content'/'versicherung' come from the shipped domains_generator.py's BOSS_DIR_DEFAULTS, not from your own project names). A ticket that doesn't match any domain (e.g. a plain software-project bug) falls through to 'default_fallback_urgency'.

escalation_rules.when: the ticket concerns a published/production software project AND the bug looks severe or breaking
escalation_rules.note: Don't guess severity from a one-line report. Send a lean, diagnosis-only sub-agent first (reads the relevant code/logs, sizes the bug, reports back compactly); act on its verdict, don't pre-judge.

escalation_rules.when: the ticket text contains one of the trigger keywords (case-insensitive)
the best-fit candidate model/device is only user-launchable (see the MODEL ROUTING / provider table)
escalation_rules.note: Urgency and routing are independent axes. A 'sofort' ticket that needs a user-only model still goes to .USER/ -- it is just flagged urgent there instead of filed quietly.

preference_model_hint._comment: Optional consult step for genuinely borderline urgency calls. Point 'command' at whatever theory-of-mind / user-preference tool your harness has (e.g. a 'decide like the user would' skill or command). Leave 'command' null to skip this step entirely -- it is not required for the urgency gate to work.
preference_model_hint.usage: Consult only when the domain default and the escalation rules disagree, or the ticket genuinely sits on a boundary. Do not consult on clear-cut cases -- that wastes the hint's budget and slows the router down.

later_sink._comment: Where 'woche'/'backlog' tickets get filed instead of spawning a sub-agent immediately. Point this at your own background task-tracking CLI/API entry point.
later_sink.note: Leave null to fall back to the ticket's DECISION LADDER item 1 (the project's own task management: TODO.md/ROADMAP.md/BUGS.md/etc.).
